## Runtime and existing test baseline

Blender 5.2.2 LTS (build hash `d13f752e3b9c`, 2026-09-15), Python 3.11.15, pytest 9.1.1, Node v24.16.0, FFmpeg/ffprobe 8.1.2 were found. The exact four plan-pinned baseline commands were run:

- Camera tests: 10 passed.
- Layer/depth suites: 117 passed, 2 failed. Both failures are isolated-worktree fixture availability: `world-tokyo-customs-dock-v1.png` is absent locally while the index points to main, and `world-tokyo-customs-dock-v1-alive.png` is absent locally. Main assets were not copied or modified.
- Rig foundation/DQS/pose-contract tests: 20 passed.
- Render-queue/catalog/store/resolver/editorial-adapter/motion-QC integration tests: 83 passed.

Read-only local AI inventory found the Hugging Face CLI and cached audio/vision models (including Depth Anything V2 and SAM2); no LoRA was confirmed. No ComfyUI command or common local install path was found. No endpoint, account, or provider call was made. Blender remains the authoring baseline; these tools are optional downstream enhancement candidates, not runtime dependencies.

## Candidate and current verdict

MPFB v2.0.17 source is pinned to commit `80919fa4682335c41847f761a4d79dcad4124732`; its local extension package SHA-256 is `923b0a0950b2b1d75440200b5457e9af9951e477b37a8e1537956f5f28b15c31`. Upstream marks code GPL-3.0-or-later and bundled assets CC0 1.0; see the source `LICENSE.md`, `LICENSE.CODE.md`, `LICENSE.ASSETS.md`, and `src/mpfb/blender_manifest.toml`. The package was built/validated from the pinned source and installed only in the ignored project-local Blender profile at `tests/fixtures/modeling/baseline/profile`. The source clone, package, and profile are ignored tool cache, not vendored source deliverables.

Three failed bounded execution attempts are recorded. Attempt 1 used the legacy source-import route, failed on extension namespace/path handling, and created four MPFB user-resource files outside the fixture; parent hash-verified and removed them. Attempts 2 and 3 used the actual packaged extension with `BLENDER_USER_RESOURCES` set to the fixture profile, `--offline-mode`, and `--disable-autoexec`. Both logs report `Human created` and `Successfully generated: "Human.rigify"`. Attempt 2 then failed in the inspection exporter because Blender 5.2 `Bone` has no `.roll` property. Attempt 3 was updated for that API and completed the script's mesh/rig/pose/deformation measurement block in memory, then failed at render setup: this Blender build exposes `BLENDER_EEVEE`, `BLENDER_WORKBENCH`, and `CYCLES`, not `BLENDER_EEVEE_NEXT`. The exact third-attempt fatal is in local review output `B/baseline/candidates/mpfb-2.0.17/inspection.json`; only this inspection JSON exists there, with no `.blend` or PNG render. MPFB's runtime log placed its config/data/cache/log directories under `F/baseline/profile`; both previously implicated global paths (`%APPDATA%\Blender Foundation\Blender\5.2\mpfb` and `...\scripts\addons\mpfb`) were absent at final recheck. No provider/service call occurred.

That was the Luna checkpoint, not the final candidate verdict. The three failed Luna attempts were escalated to GPT-6 Sol xhigh without resetting the count. Sol attempt 4 saved a `.blend`, inspection report, and two PNGs but animated an FK control while the rig's `IK_FK` switch was 0, leaving the deform bone and mesh static; the default Cube obscured the figure. Read-only inspection of the saved rig established that the active IK chain overrode FK. Sol attempt 5 used the same event/pose fixture with `IK_FK=1`, hid the Cube, and passed: `DEF-upper_arm.R` tail moved 0.0715166 m; 4,736 of 13,380 evaluated Human vertices moved more than 1e-5 m (max 0.3319437 m, mean 0.0623227 m); Human ground minimum was approximately 0 m. The full figure is visible in both saved views; the opposite-estimate view is visually front. Source, script, fixture and artifact hashes are in `benchmark-inputs.json`. No global MPFB paths were observed on final check.

The saved `Human` mesh inventory reports 19,158 stored vertices and 18,486 polygons. The 13,380 figure above is the evaluated-vertex sample used by the deformation check, not the stored mesh budget. Triangle count and any final subdivided/sculpted render mesh remain unmeasured; vendor polygon/triangle targets must not be compared directly to that 13,380-vertex sample. The next art/shot benchmark should record stored and evaluated vertices, faces and triangles separately, then inspect close-up silhouette, face/hands, impact-pose deformation and render cost at multiple detail levels.

**T1 selection:** MPFB 2.0.17 + Blender Rigify passes the offline editable-human/rig/control/deformation starter fixture and is selected for T4a authoring work. This is not an accepted fighter model: the white default human has no recognizable caricature, finished face/hands/materials, stress-pose review, believable strike/fall, or operator visual approval. The local LoRA/Hugging Face/ComfyUI path and Blender MCP are optional downstream/interactive routes; neither was needed or used for this reproducible starter probe. The two unrelated Tokyo PNG fixture failures remain documented, not silently counted as passes.
